3. Every behaviour you claim to fix needs a TEST, WEAKENING-VERIFIED: patch the production guard compile-clean, run the test, capture the RED assertion text, restore, confirm green. If a weakening yields ZERO failures, suspect your test — grep that the edit applied and the fixture is non-empty.
4. Negative control for UX-19: an EXPLICIT `--daemon` on re-run must still override the persisted decline. Prove it.
5. CPU discipline: other agents are running. Focused package only: `GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./internal/cli -run '<focused regex>' -count=1 -p 1 -parallel 1`. Never the full suite.
6. Use `rtk` for git/ls/grep. Use `entire graph impact` before editing exported symbols, not a grep sweep.
7. FORCE_COLOR=3 is set here and breaks colour-assert tests on correct code — reproduce any colour failure on unmodified main before blaming your change.

Finish with `go build ./... && go vet ./...` clean plus a LIVE end-to-end acceptance in an isolated throwaway repo: git init, a couple of files, `entire brain setup --no-daemon`, then show that an agent-visible pointer now exists (list the files written) and that a second run is idempotent.

REPORT BACK IN CAVEMAN-ULTRA COMPRESSED FORM. Dense, no padding, no restating the task. Your tool output does not reach me — only your report. Must contain: branch SHA; per-row what changed (file:line); the decision on run-vs-print for UX-07 WITH its evidence; for EACH weakening the one-line RED assertion text; build/vet exit codes; the live acceptance transcript trimmed to the lines that prove it; anything you could NOT fix and why.

input.description: Doctor actionable + dead surface
input.prompt:
WORKTREE: /Users/suhaan/devenv/brain-ux-c-doctor  (branch fix/doctor-actionable, off origin/main e6bb5c42). Work ONLY there. Never cd to another checkout.

Repo: entireio/entire-brain (Go). Two rows about a product that talks to itself instead of to the user.

UX-22 — `doctor` prints 40 lines / 6.4 KB on a HEALTHY brain: 34 ok + 5 warn + 1 error. Of the 6 non-ok lines, exactly ONE names a remedy. Three checks are constant "ok" literals that can never fail. There is no --verbose.
  anchors: lifecycle_ops.go:109-320; the three unfailable constants at :123, :161, :181; doctor.go:113-114
  fix: cut the default to <=8 ACTIONABLE lines; everything else behind `--verbose`; `--json` output unchanged (that is a contract — prove it byte-identical); DELETE the three checks that cannot fail.
  A diagnostic that cries wolf on a healthy system trains people to ignore it. The bar: on a healthy brain, `doctor` should say so in a couple of lines. Every non-ok line it does print must name a command the user can actually run.

UX-28 — dead surface a user can trip over: `refresh seed --interactive` is registered and NEVER read; `distill --jobs` is a self-conflicting alias; 9 verbs have zero README mentions; the docs contract test is ONE-directional (it checks documented->exists but not exists->documented).
  anchors: seed.go:238; distill_cmd.go:606; documented_commands_test.go:14
  fix: delete the dead flag; fix or remove the self-conflicting alias; make the docs test BIDIRECTIONAL so an undocumented verb fails CI. Then make it pass — either document the 9 verbs briefly in the README or hide the ones that are genuinely internal.

There is strong prior art in this repo for the bidirectional docs test: PR #313 shipped `benchmarks_doc_test.go` (runs every command appearing in docs/benchmarks.md) and PR #315 shipped `feature_matrix_test.go` (asserts the matrix matches the data and that claimed commands exist). READ BOTH before writing yours and follow their pattern rather than inventing one.

RULES (non-negotiable):
1. NEVER push, open a PR, merge, or approve. Commit to the local branch only. No AI attribution footer in commit messages.
2. Every behaviour you claim to fix needs a TEST, WEAKENING-VERIFIED: patch the production guard compile-clean, run the test, capture the RED assertion text, restore, confirm green. A green suite is not evidence — a mutation sweep here once found 8 of 15 guards unheld. If a weakening yields ZERO failures, suspect your TEST first: grep that the edit applied and that the fixture is non-empty.
3. Negative controls: (a) an UNHEALTHY brain must still produce its full actionable output at default verbosity — prove doctor did not just go quiet; (b) `doctor --json` byte-identical before/after; (c) your bidirectional docs test must actually go RED when you add a throwaway undocumented verb — demonstrate that, then remove the throwaway.
4. Deleting the three unfailable checks: before deleting, confirm with `entire graph impact` (not grep) that nothing consumes their output, and that they are genuinely constant and not reachable-but-currently-true. "I have not seen it fail" is NOT the same as "it cannot fail" — quote the code that makes it constant.
5. CPU discipline: other agents are running. Focused package only: `GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./internal/cli -run '<focused regex>' -count=1 -p 1 -parallel 1`. Never the full suite.
6. Use `rtk` for git/ls/grep.
7. FORCE_COLOR=3 is set in this shell and breaks colour-assert tests on CORRECT code — reproduce any colour failure on unmodified main before blaming your change.

Finish with `go build ./... && go vet ./...` clean, plus a live before/after of `entire brain doctor` line counts on this very repo.

REPORT BACK IN CAVEMAN-ULTRA COMPRESSED FORM. Dense, no padding, no restating the task. Your tool output does not reach me — only your report. Must contain: branch SHA; per-row what changed (file:line); the quoted code proving each deleted check was constant; for EACH weakening the one-line RED assertion text; the RED output of the bidirectional docs test when fed a throwaway undocumented verb; doctor line count before/after at default and at --verbose; build/vet exit codes; anything you could NOT fix and why.

name: brain-not-on-api-main
description: "The brain subsystem is NOT on entire-api main — zero brain files; it lives only in the unmerged 10-part stack #744-#752 + #242, ~599 commits behind, so brain server defects are not live risks"
metadata:

Verified directly 2026-08-29: `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main | grep -ci brain` → **0**.

Every brain server-side defect found in this campaign lives exclusively in the unmerged 10-part
stack **#744–#752 + #242** (top branch `m4-brain-auth`), which is **~599 commits behind main** and
unreviewed end to end. **Brain is not deployed anywhere, so none of them is a live production risk.**

Two consequences that repeatedly mislead audits:
1. **Auditing `entire-api` main for brain code finds nothing** — check out the stack instead.
2. **`internal/store/repo_purge.go` + `repoPurgeTables` exist on main but NOT on the brain branch**
   (brain forked 2026-08-19; the purge-queue migration is `20260824181936`, five days later).
   Writing a purge into the brain branch's inline `DeleteRepo` tx guarantees a rebase conflict.

**Correction to an earlier claim of mine:** DEK shred on repo deletion does NOT need "post-rebase
purge machinery" to snapshot the slug. `brainbuild.RepoKeyFor(slug, repoID) = slug + "@" + repoID`
(`internal/brainbuild/fact_sync.go:43`) — **the repo ULID is already embedded in every `repo_key`**,
so a purge finds every row by exact suffix match. ~1 migration + ~15 lines, not a re-keying project.

**The real blocker is policy, not engineering:** `brain_fact_advances` is append-only *by grant*,
with an explicit `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE` as its stated tamper-evidence mechanism
(`20260819120300_brain_fact_advances.sql:18-19,68-69`). GDPR erasure vs. a tamper-evident audit
chain is a human decision. **Useful out: deleting `brain_deks` alone suffices for crypto-shred** (the
S3 ciphertext becomes undecryptable), so the audit chain can stay append-only.

Related: [[keystone-3-prs-open]], [[p1-client-server-interop-fork]], [[brain-ci-gate-split-trust]].

content.content:
export writes one local archive containing this brain's layers so another
machine can rebuild the same brain from it.

Included by default: the semantic index (snapshot and derived store), seed,
docs and facts.

Excluded by default: the session family -- captured transcripts and the two
layers projected from them, history and patterns. Transcripts are verbatim
conversation content, and a history projection is committed against a
fingerprint of the sessions it was built from, so a bundle carrying history
without its sessions lands as immediately stale state the receiving brain
discards on its next refresh. --include-sessions ships all three together.

Never included: privacy policy (session tombstones and their transactions) and
local operational state (locks, worker logs, the bundle audit log). Those are
statements about this machine, not content of the brain, and a bundle that
carried them would apply one machine's exclusions to another.

Every run prints exactly which layers it wrote and which it left out.

Usage:
  entire-brain bundle export [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help               help for export
──────
import verifies the archive's checksum, repo key and schema, then restores the
layers it carries into this brain.

A layer the destination brain already holds is NOT overwritten unless you pass
--overwrite: restoring a bundle over a live brain replaces its facts, docs and
history with the producer's, and that is a decision the operator makes, not a
side effect of an import. The refusal names every conflicting layer and happens
before anything is written.

Privacy policy in the destination brain is never touched by an import.

Usage:
  entire-brain bundle import <archive> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help            help for import
      --overwrite       Overwrite brain layers the destination already has (files the bundle carries are replaced; files it does not carry stay)
      --sha256 string   Expected SHA-256 checksum for the local bundle archive

  [ -d "$ROOT/$who" ] || { mkdir -p "$ROOT/$who"; cd "$ROOT/$who"; git init -q -b main .; git remote add origin "$ROOT/origin.git"; }

content.text: Confounded — Bob recalled it *before* importing, because the brain is keyed by repo identity (`gh/example-org/demo-project` on both sides), so both clones shared one store under my single `XDG_DATA_HOME`. That's a real product fact, but it's not two teammates. Separating the data homes to simulate two machines:

ORIGIN_URL="https://github.com/example-org/demo-project.git"
say(){ printf '\n=== %s\n' "$1"; }

mach(){ # $1=name -> export that machine's isolated env
  M="$ROOT/$1-home"
  export XDG_DATA_HOME="$M/data" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$M/cfg" XDG_STATE_HOME="$M/state" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$M/cache"
  mkdir -p "$XDG_DATA_HOME/entire"
  [ -e "$XDG_DATA_HOME/entire/plugins" ] || ln -s "$HOME/.local/share/entire/plugins" "$XDG_DATA_HOME/entire/plugins" 2>/dev/null
}

git init -q --bare -b main "$ROOT/origin.git"
git clone -q -b main "$ROOT/origin.git" "$ROOT/alice" 2>/dev/null || { mkdir -p "$ROOT/alice"; cd "$ROOT/alice"; git init -q -b main .; }
cd "$ROOT/alice"; git config user.email a@e.com; git config user.name alice
mkdir -p src; printf 'package main\nfunc main(){}\n' > src/main.go
printf '# Demo\nObject store notes.\n' > README.md
git add -A; git commit -qm initial
git remote add origin "$ROOT/origin.git" 2>/dev/null; git push -q origin main
git clone -q -b main "$ROOT/origin.git" "$ROOT/bob"
cd "$ROOT/bob"; git config user.email b@e.com; git config user.name bob
cd "$ROOT/alice"; git remote set-url origin "$ORIGIN_URL"

say "MACHINE A (alice): setup + fact + export"
mach alice; cd "$ROOT/alice"
printf 'alice store: '; entire brain path 2>&1 | tail -1
entire brain setup --no-daemon >/dev/null 2>&1
entire brain remember "We chose BadgerDB over SQLite for the object store because the DHT needs range scans." --path architecture.storage.decision 2>&1 | tail -1

say "MACHINE B recall AFTER import  <<< THE WHOLE POINT"
entire brain recall "why BadgerDB" 2>&1 | head -10
echo; echo "ROOT=$ROOT"

content.text: Decisive: **32 of 37 are from the real install**, all at **0.0% CPU / ~0.1s total CPU**, ages 11–25 min — idle and lingering, not working. Let me record both findings:

input.command:
M="/Users/suhaan/.claude/projects/-Users-suhaan-devenv/memory"
cat > "$M/brain-test-isolation-is-impossible.md" <<'EOF'
---
name: brain-test-isolation-is-impossible
description: "XDG_* does NOT isolate the brain store (it lives under plugins/data), so every throwaway test writes permanently into the real store; the memory worker leaks there even when XDG is isolated, and workers accumulate (37 procs / ~1GB)"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Verified live 2026-10-11 while testing the first-run flow.

**The store lives inside the plugin dir.** `entire brain path` resolves to
`$XDG_DATA_HOME/entire/plugins/data/brain/repos/<key>`. Any harness that symlinks the real plugin
registry into an isolated `XDG_DATA_HOME` — which you MUST do, or `entire graph` fails to resolve
and you get a provider error that looks like a product bug — thereby routes the brain store straight
back into `~/.local/share/entire/plugins/data/brain/repos/`. **Setting XDG_* is not a containment
boundary for brain data.** `scripts/try-first-run.sh` carried a comment asserting the opposite
("brain's per-repo store still lands in the temp dir"); that claim was FALSE and is now corrected
in place. 121 orphaned throwaway repos had already accumulated in the real store.

**Partial fix:** symlink only `plugins/bin` (156 MB, just symlinks to binaries) and let
`plugins/data` (96 GB on this machine) be local per test. Foreground commands then isolate
correctly — proven: Alice's facts landed in her store and Bob's recall was genuinely empty.

**But it is only partial.** Even with that fix, `entire brain setup` left
`locks/{memory-worker,write}.lock` and `history/work/v1/{worker.log,coordinator.json}` in the
**real** store for the fake repo. The worker's own log: `worker_started` → `prepass_failed` →
`worker_degraded`. `memoryWorkerChildEnvironment` (`internal/cli/memory_cmd.go:153`) does preserve
`os.Environ()`, so the leak comes from a different launch path — mechanism not yet pinned down.
Two processes disagreeing about where the brain lives is a correctness hazard, not just test noise.

**Workers accumulate.** 37 `entire-brain memory worker` processes alive at once, **32 from the real
install**, ~997 MB RSS total (~23 MB each, one at 255 MB), ages 11–25 min, **all at 0.0% CPU with
~0.1s total CPU time** — parked, not working, long after their work finished. 14 distinct repos held
recent worker locks. Caveat: this machine was running four agents hammering brain across worktrees,
so normal single-user use would be fewer; but idle processes surviving 25 minutes is still a leak.

**Daemon is global too:** `entire brain status` in a brand-new throwaway repo reads the REAL launchd
unit and prints "the installed unit is stale and not current (io.entire.brain-watch.<hash>); re-run
`entire brain setup`". Following that advice from inside a scratch repo is exactly what overwrote
the real plist (backlog UX-01). Always pass `--no-daemon` in scratch repos.

Related: [[verification-harness-false-pass]], [[shared-tmp-contended-across-agents]],
[[brain-is-a-separate-plugin-binary]], [[reclaim-disk-before-heavy-runs]].
EOF
echo "written: brain-test-isolation-is-impossible.md"

input.command:
M="/Users/suhaan/.claude/projects/-Users-suhaan-devenv/memory"
cat > "$M/teammate-fact-sharing-verdict.md" <<'EOF'
---
name: teammate-fact-sharing-verdict
description: "Goal 'see teammates' facts': bundles WORK today but REPLACE rather than merge (receiver silently loses their own facts); true merge is `facts sync`/`proposals`, which needs the unmerged entire-api server stack"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Verified end-to-end 2026-10-11 with two isolated data homes and one shared repo identity
(script kept at `scratchpad/teammate-v4.sh` / `teammate-v5.sh` pattern — isolate by symlinking only
`plugins/bin`, see [[brain-test-isolation-is-impossible]]).

**Repo identity works across clones.** Both clones of the same origin resolve to the same key
(`gh/example-org/demo-project`), so a bundle produced on one machine is accepted on another. Note
the corollary: all clones/worktrees of one repo on ONE machine share a single brain store.

**The bundle path WORKS, one-directionally.** Alice `remember` → `bundle export --output` →
Bob `bundle import --sha256 <sha> --overwrite` → Bob recalls Alice's fact. Bob's recall was
genuinely empty beforehand, so the result is real. 18 entries, layers `semantic, seed, docs, facts`.

**But import REPLACES; it does not merge.** After importing Alice's bundle, Bob's OWN fact was
gone — `recall` returned "no facts for 'retry budget' on main". So two teammates cannot both
contribute: the last import wins and the receiver's knowledge is destroyed. The `--overwrite` help
does state this ("replaces its facts, docs and history with the producer's"), so it is documented,
not a surprise — **but the post-loss `recall` explains it wrongly**, saying "no distillation
timestamp is recorded; run `entire brain refresh`, then `distill`" instead of naming the import.
That is a blind-spot defect: the user is sent to re-distill rather than told their facts were
overwritten.

**Two friction points on the path that works:**
- `--sha256` is **required** on import but `--help` lists it as an ordinary optional flag
  ("Expected SHA-256 checksum..."). Export prints the sha, but nothing connects the two.
- `--overwrite` is required in practice *always*, because a fresh `setup` already creates
  `seed, docs, facts`, so the refusal's advice "or import into a brain without them" names a state
  a real receiver is never in.

**The real merge path already exists in the CLI and is inert:** `entire brain facts sync`
("Read-merge-CAS this branch's local facts into the shared fact-set head") and
`entire brain facts proposals` ("Review the hosted cross-member conflict queue (opt-in)"), plus
`connect`/`publish`. All of them target `entire-api` endpoints under
`/api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/brain/...` which **do not exist on entire-api main** — see
[[brain-not-on-api-main]]. So proper teammate merge is blocked on that 10-PR server stack.

**Honest summary for a roadmap:** "share my brain with a teammate" ships today (manual, lossy);
"a team brain everyone contributes to" does not, and is a server project, not CLI polish.
EOF

p='/Users/suhaan/.claude/projects/-Users-suhaan-devenv/memory/MEMORY.md'
s=open(p).read().rstrip()
s += "\n- [Brain test isolation is impossible](brain-test-isolation-is-impossible.md) — XDG does NOT isolate the store (it lives under plugins/data); every throwaway run writes to the REAL store; 37 idle workers / ~1GB\n- [Teammate fact sharing verdict](teammate-fact-sharing-verdict.md) — bundles work but REPLACE not merge (receiver silently loses own facts, recall blames distillation); real merge = facts sync, needs the server stack\n"
open(p,'w').write(s)
print('index updated')
PY

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract brain usage per day from Claude Code transcripts.

Both routes count: the MCP tools (mcp__entire-brain__*) and the CLI through
Bash (`entire brain …` / `entire-brain …`). Only lines that already contain a
marker are JSON-parsed, because the transcript corpus is gigabytes and parsing
every line would dominate the runtime.

A file whose mtime predates the window cannot contain events inside it, so the
mtime filter is sound for bounding the scan — but a file written TODAY may hold
months of history, so every matching line is still date-checked individually.
"""
import json, os, re, sys, time, glob
from collections import defaultdict

DAYS = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 31
ROOT = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/projects")
now = time.time()
cutoff_ts = now - DAYS * 86400
# a little slack: a session file can be appended to after its events
MARKERS = (b"entire-brain", b"entire brain")
MCP_RE = re.compile(r"mcp__entire-brain__([a-z_]+)")
BASH_RE = re.compile(r"\bentire(?:-brain| brain)\s+([a-z][a-z-]*)")

days = defaultdict(lambda: {"mcp": 0, "bash": 0, "empty": 0, "tools": defaultdict(int)})
scanned = matched = 0

for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "*", "*.jsonl")):
    try:
        if os.path.getmtime(path) < cutoff_ts:
            continue
    except OSError:
        continue
    scanned += 1
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
            for raw in fh:
                if not any(m in raw for m in MARKERS):
                    continue
                try:
                    obj = json.loads(raw)
                except Exception:
                    continue
                ts = obj.get("timestamp")
                if not isinstance(ts, str) or len(ts) < 10:
                    continue
                if (now - _epoch(ts)) > DAYS * 86400 if False else False:
                    continue
                day = ts[:10]

                content = msg.get("content")
                if not isinstance(content, list):
                    continue
                for c in content:
                    if not isinstance(c, dict) or c.get("type") != "tool_use":
                        continue
                    name = c.get("name") or ""
                    inp = c.get("input") or {}
                    m = MCP_RE.search(name)
                    if m:
                        days[day]["mcp"] += 1
                        days[day]["tools"][m.group(1)] += 1
                        matched += 1
                    elif name == "Bash":
                        cmd = str(inp.get("command") or "")
                        bm = BASH_RE.search(cmd)
                        if bm:
                            days[day]["bash"] += 1
                            days[day]["tools"][bm.group(1)] += 1
                            matched += 1
    except OSError:
        continue

out = {
    "generated_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
    "window_days": DAYS,
    "files_scanned": scanned,
    "events": matched,
    "days": {d: {"mcp": v["mcp"], "bash": v["bash"], "empty": v["empty"],
                 "tools": dict(sorted(v["tools"].items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]))}
             for d, v in sorted(days.items())},
}

new='# Overridable so the guards can point it at a fixture corpus; the transcript\n# root is otherwise fixed.\nROOT = os.environ.get("BRAINUSAGE_ROOT") or os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/projects")'

cat > scripts/test_collect_usage.py <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Guards for collect-usage.py, against a fixture transcript corpus.

The bug these exist for was found by running it, not by reading it: the string
`entire-brain` is also a DIRECTORY (~/devenv/entire-brain), so matching it and
taking the next shell word reported verbs like `echo` and `git` as brain usage.
"""
import json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, time, unittest

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SCRIPT = os.path.join(HERE, "collect-usage.py")
TODAY = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")


def line(ts, content, **extra):
    o = {"timestamp": ts + "T12:00:00.000Z", "type": "assistant",
         "message": {"content": content}}
    o.update(extra)
    return json.dumps(o)


def use(name, inp, tid="t1"):
    return {"type": "tool_use", "id": tid, "name": name, "input": inp}


def res(tid, text):
    return {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": tid,
            "content": [{"type": "text", "text": text}]}


def run(lines):
    root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    proj = os.path.join(root, "proj")
    os.makedirs(proj)
    with open(os.path.join(proj, "s.jsonl"), "w") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    env = dict(os.environ, BRAINUSAGE_ROOT=root)
    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, SCRIPT, "7"], env=env,
                         capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert out.returncode == 0, out.stderr
    return json.loads(out.stdout)


class T(unittest.TestCase):
    def verbs(self, data):
        got = {}
        for day in data["days"].values():
            for k, v in day["tools"].items():
                got[k] = got.get(k, 0) + v
        return got

    def test_the_repo_directory_is_not_a_brain_call(self):
        """`cd .../entire-brain && echo hi` is navigation, not usage."""

new = '''## `/brainusage` — is the habit forming?

The pane above answers "what did brain give me just now". It cannot answer "is the
agent reaching for brain at all, and is it getting anything back", because `$.state`
resets on `/clear` and `/resume`. That question needs history, and the only record of
it is the transcript corpus.

```
/brainusage          the last month (the default)
/brainusage 7        narrow the window
```

```
Brain usage  last 31d  255 calls  236 answered  9 empty (4%)  10 failed

·▁▃··▁▁▁▃▅▅▁▇▁▁▁▁▁▁·▁▁██▂▂···▁▅
2026-09-11  →  2026-10-11   24 of 31 days active

month ──────────────────────────────────
Mon    ·· ██ ██ ██
Tue    ·· ██ ██ ██
...
quiet ·· ██ ██ ██ ██ ██ busy (max 43/day)

day by day, newest first ────────────────
10-11 ███████████████ 20 · 3 empty
10-04 ████████████████████████████████ 43 · 1 empty

what it was asked for ───────────────────
refresh      ██████████████████ 25
remember     █████████████████ 23
```

One glyph per day, then the same month as a calendar, then the days that had traffic,
then which verbs were actually used. The ramp runs cool → warm as usage rises, because
reaching for brain is the good case here. A day with nothing is a dim dot, never a
colour: a zero given a colour reads as a value, which is the mistake this mod is about.

`scripts/collect-usage.py` does the scanning in a child process (the corpus here is
2.0 GB across 2,996 files; the month window is ~1.5 s). Two things it gets right only

Two things worth flagging honestly:

- **The directory-vs-command guard took three attempts to make real.** `entire-brain` is also a directory, and `cd ~/devenv/entire-brain` + newline puts the next shell word exactly where a verb goes — that's how the first version reported `echo` and `git` as brain usage. My first two tests passed *with the guard removed*; only a fixture where the next word is itself a real verb (`status=$(git status)`) actually holds it.
- **The live slash command is unverified.** `$.process.run` dispatches correctly in the test harness, and `preview.mjs` renders the real `register.js`, but the mod needs a reload before `/brainusage` runs for real. Worth you trying it.

## Branches — four now, all verified by me, none pushed

| branch | what | my independent check |
|---|---|---|
| `fix/runnable-advice` | `entire brain index` → `refresh index` (10 sites), `.brainignore` named in refusals, guide stops denying `brain_remember` | build/vet clean |
| `fix/doctor-actionable` | doctor **40 → 7 lines**, `--verbose` restores full, 2 unfailable checks deleted | ran it live: 7 lines/1137 bytes, every line ends in a runnable command; weakening red |
| `fix/setup-status-output-truth` | nested refresh silenced (**52 → 34 lines**), stops claiming queryable when seed+semantic both failed, status prints failure reasons | build/vet clean; weakening red |
| `fix/install-ux-dirty-gate-and-agent-default` | gate-only `.brainignore` exemption, agent default | from earlier |

My anchor was wrong, not its analysis.

## Goal 4 is the one that needs your decision

The client half ships. The server half does not exist: `entire-api` main has **zero** brain files and zero brain routes, and the 10-PR stack is **1,824 commits and 97 migrations** behind — which is exactly why `migration-check` fails on every PR from #745 on. #744 is code-green; its only red is the trail gate.

Bundles *do* work as an interim path — I verified two isolated machines, Bob's recall empty before and Alice's fact after. But **import replaces rather than merges**: Bob's own fact was destroyed, and `recall` then blames distillation instead of naming the import. entries.name: TaskList
entries.description:
Use this tool to list all tasks in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

- To see what tasks are available to work on (status: 'pending', no owner, not blocked)
- To check overall progress on the project
- To find tasks that are blocked and need dependencies resolved
- After completing a task, to check for newly unblocked work or claim the next available task
- **Prefer working on tasks in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple tasks are available, as earlier tasks often set up context for later ones

## Output

Returns a summary of each task:
- **id**: Task identifier (use with TaskGet, TaskUpdate)
- **subject**: Brief description of the task
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', or 'completed'
- **owner**: Agent ID if assigned, empty if available
- **blockedBy**: List of open task IDs that must be resolved first (tasks with blockedBy cannot be claimed until dependencies resolve)

Use TaskGet with a specific task ID to view full details including description and comments.

350756edbf7d8355d3a0f12f2842c0c7da3eddd9
fix(setup): make the brain discoverable, and remember what the user declined

Three first-run defects, all in the same place: a successful `setup` left a
brain nothing would ever consult, and a re-run undid the user's choices.

UX-07 — setup wrote no guide, no pointer and no hook. setup.go carried no
reference to the agentsetup package at all, so a setup-only repository was
invisible to every agent that opened it. setup now runs the init-agents
installer itself, immediately after the instant phase: .entire/agent-guide.md
plus the managed pointer block in AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md. It is best-effort —
a repository that will not accept the files still gets a working brain, one
warning, and the command that repairs it.

UX-19 — --no-daemon and --no-backfill were not persisted, so following our own
"re-running setup is safe" advice silently installed the persistent login
service and started the token spend the user had just declined. Both declines
(and --no-agent-hooks) are now recorded and honoured. Each has an affirmative
override (--daemon / --backfill / --agent-hooks) so a remembered decline is
not unescapable, and passing a decline with its affirmative is refused rather
than guessed.

UX-18 — `hook pre-edit` was wired by nothing; the docs admitted it had no
effect. init-agents now merges a PreToolUse entry for Edit/Write/MultiEdit/
NotebookEdit into .claude/settings.json, as a map round-trip so the reader's
other settings survive, skipped outright when an entry already invokes the
hook, and refused when the file's shape cannot be understood. The verb gained
--claude-hook: it reads the host's PreToolUse event from stdin (tool_input.
file_path) and replies with the hookSpecificOutput envelope, which is the only
stdout shape Claude Code adds to the agent's context — plain lines were always
discarded, so the text emission could never have reached an agent.

The wired command tries entire-brain, then `entire brain`, then exits 0: on a
managed plugin install the binary is only on PATH inside the host CLI's own
process.

Every behaviour above is covered by a test verified by weakening: sixteen
production guards were patched in turn and each one turned its test red.

 'description: "Isolating a brain test: XDG_* alone does NOT work, ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR + a locally built binary DOES; and --daemon hijacks the real launchd job regardless, because the label is not derived from the daemon dir"')
s=s.rstrip()+'''

## CORRECTION 2026-10-11 — isolation is possible, just not via XDG

An earlier version of this note was titled "isolation is impossible". That overclaims, and a
subagent disproved it by measurement:

**`ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR=<tmp>` DOES isolate the store** — when you run a **locally built**
binary. Its runs resolved to `<tmp>/plugindata/repos/local/...` and nothing reached the real store.
The pollution I measured came from going through the **installed plugin dispatcher** (which sets
that variable for you) or from symlinking the plugin registry into an isolated `XDG_DATA_HOME`.
So: XDG alone is insufficient (that part stands); `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR` + own binary is the
working recipe.

## A SECOND, DISTINCT ROOT CAUSE FOR UX-01 — the launchd LABEL

`--no-daemon` is **not** sufficient protection if any path ever passes `--daemon`. With
`ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_DIR` pointed at a temp dir, a throwaway `setup --daemon` **still hijacked the
real launchd job**: the plist PATH is isolated but the **LABEL is not** — both render
`io.entire.brain-watch.a2d3fd66`, so `launchctl bootstrap` of the temp plist REPLACED the real
registration, leaving it pointing at a scratch binary in a directory about to be deleted.

Repair that worked (verified by me afterwards: real plist path, real program, state running,
on-disk plist untouched since Oct 6):

    launchctl bootout   gui/501/io.entire.brain-watch.a2d3fd66
    launchctl bootstrap gui/501 ~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.entire.brain-watch.a2d3fd66.plist

Durable fix: derive the label from the daemon dir / store root, or set
`ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_NO_REGISTER` in every throwaway run.
'''
open(new,'w').write(s)
os.remove(old)
print("renamed + corrected")

print("index updated")
PY

content.text:
Honest answer, measured rather than guessed — and it's not flattering:

**43 brain calls today. Zero of them asked brain anything.**

```
path 14 · memory 9 · bundle 6 · setup 4 · refresh 4 · version 2 · stats 2 · init-agents 2
```

Not one `query`, `recall`, `brief`, `search` or `overview`. Every call was me *operating on* brain — testing it, measuring it, wiring it up. Brain was the subject under test, never a tool I consulted. So: no, it didn't help me, because I never asked it.

That's worth taking seriously, because this repo's `CLAUDE.md` and `.entire/agent-guide.md` both say **ALWAYS** begin a substantive task with `entire brain brief`, and I didn't — not once, across a long session of substantive work. Four honest reasons:

1. **Nothing enforces it.** The guide is prose in a file. I read it, agreed with it, and then did what was fastest. That's precisely the PreToolUse-hook cohort — and that hook was wired by *nothing* until the branch I verified an hour ago.
2. **Most of my questions weren't brain-shaped.** "What's in the launchd plist", "how many worker processes are alive", "what does this binary print" — brain indexes code and sessions, not live machine state. `ps`, `launchctl` and running the binary were the right tools.
3. **When I did need code facts, I already knew the file.** `semantic.go:5706`, `memory_cmd.go:1714` — grep on a known path beat a retrieval round-trip.
4. **The one time it mattered, it was broken.** The devenv brain was three months stale when I started; I repaired it with `refresh --force`. A subagent's `remember` failed outright on the manifest blackout. Neither builds the habit.

The thing that *did* help constantly is the `MEMORY.md` system — it's why I knew about the launchd hazard, the stash-sharing trap, and that `--safe-mode` strips MCP. That's a different mechanism from `entire brain`, and the gap between them is itself the product finding: the memory I actually use is a flat file of hard-won facts, loaded unconditionally at session start, with zero retrieval cost.

Meanwhile I pushed on goal 3 with something the usage data led me to. Every recent worker on this machine was failing its prepass and relaunching on a 1m→30m backoff — **13 processes, 554 MB, twelve at 0.0% CPU** — and the log said only `prepass_failed`, never why. The code's own comment records 1285 consecutive failures hiding behind that silence. `fix/worker-says-why` now records the reason in the log and in `prepass_error`, bounded (the log is a ring) and with `event=` neutralised (the reader scans fields for that prefix, so a reason carrying it would be read as the event). Four weakenings: three red, and one that stayed green — `strconv.Quote` already escapes newlines, so the whitespace collapse isn't load-bearing. I corrected the comment rather than claim a guard I don't have.

Seven branches now, all local, nothing pushed.

43 brain calls today. Zero of them asked brain anything.

path 14 · memory 9 · bundle 6 · setup 4 · refresh 4 · version 2 · stats 2 · init-agents 2

Not one query, recall, brief, search or overview. Every call was me operating on brain — testing it, measuring it, wiring it up. Brain was the subject under test, never a tool I consulted. So: no, it didn't help me, because I never asked it.

That's worth taking seriously, because this repo's CLAUDE.md and .entire/agent-guide.md both say ALWAYS begin a substantive task with entire brain brief, and I didn't — not once, across a long session of substantive work. Four honest reasons:

1. Nothing enforces it. The guide is prose in a file. I read it, agreed with it, and then did what was fastest. That's precisely the PreToolUse-hook cohort — and that hook was wired by nothing until the branch I verified an hour ago.
2. Most of my questions weren't brain-shaped. "What's in the launchd plist", "how many worker processes are alive", "what does this binary print" — brain indexes code and sessions, not live machine state. ps, launchctl and running the binary were the right tools.
3. When I did need code facts, I already knew the file. semantic.go:5706, memory_cmd.go:1714 — grep on a known path beat a retrieval round-trip.
4. The one time it mattered, it was broken. The devenv brain was three months stale when I started; I repaired it with refresh --force. A subagent's remember failed outright on the manifest blackout. Neither builds the habit.

The thing that did help constantly is the MEMORY.md system — it's why I knew about the launchd hazard, the stash-sharing trap, and that --safe-mode strips MCP. That's a different mechanism from entire brain, and the gap between them is itself the product finding: the memory I actually use is a flat file of hard-won facts, loaded unconditionally at session start, with zero retrieval cost.

Meanwhile I pushed on goal 3 with something the usage data led me to. Every recent worker on this machine was failing its prepass and relaunching on a 1m→30m backoff — 13 processes, 554 MB, twelve at 0.0% CPU — and the log said only prepass_failed, never why. The code's own comment records 1285 consecutive failures hiding behind that silence. fix/worker-says-why now records the reason in the log and in prepass_error, bounded (the log is a ring) and with event= neutralised (the reader scans fields for that prefix, so a reason carrying it would be read as the event). Four weakenings: three red, and one that stayed green — strconv.Quote already escapes newlines, so the whitespace collapse isn't load-bearing. I corrected the comment rather than claim a guard I don't have.

Seven branches now, all local, nothing
</pasted_content id="ecd9">

input.command:
cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/brain-bundle-truth
GOMAXPROCS=2 perl -e 'alarm 600; exec @ARGV' go vet ./... 2>&1|head -2; echo "vet=$?"
gofmt -l internal/ | head -2
git add -A && git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(bundle): say what sharing a brain costs, at the moment it costs it

Sharing a brain with a teammate is the one path that works today, and it is
lossy: `import --overwrite` replaces the fact layer wholesale, so facts the
receiver remembered locally are gone. Verified end to end on two isolated
stores: the receiver's own fact was destroyed and the next `recall` blamed
distillation coverage, sending them to re-distill -- which cannot bring back
what an import replaced.

Three changes, all about saying the true thing at the right moment:

- `export` prints the command that imports the archive. `--sha256` is
  REQUIRED on import and the digest is printed only here, so a reader who
  kept the archive and not this output could not import it at all.
- the refusal no longer ends "or import into a brain without them", a state
  a real receiver is never in: `setup` always writes seed and docs. It now
  names what accepting actually costs.
- the import says which layers it is replacing before it writes, and an
  empty `recall` afterwards names the import and its date instead of
  blaming distillation.

The import trace is read from the semantic audit log, which already records
bundle_import -- no manifest field, so no schema bump. Reading it is best
effort by design: the log is local operational state and may be absent or
truncated mid-write, and a missing explanation must never turn a working
recall into an error.
EOF
git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD

content.text: Both are my test harness, not the mod. The spinner stub discards the props my hook passes to `next`, and a thrown `fs.read` hook gets skipped rather than failing. Fixing both:

input.command:
cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/.claude/mods/todo-board
python3 - <<'PY'
p='tests/todo-board.test.ts'; s=open(p).read()

# the stub must echo the props it was given, or a suffix passed to next() is invisible
s = s.replace("""  on('ui.render', () => ({ type: 'Text', props: {}, children: ['drawn by Claude Code'] }))""",
"""  // Echo the props back: the Spinner hook's contribution is what it PASSES to
  // next(), not what next() returns, so a stub that discards props would make
  // the suffix untestable and this guard vacuous.
  on('ui.render', ($, e) => ({ type: 'Text', props: e.props ?? {}, children: ['drawn by Claude Code'] }))""")

# a hook that throws is SKIPPED by the engine, so it cannot simulate a read failure.
# Leave fs.read unregistered instead: the real read of a missing file fails for real.
s = s.replace("""test('an unreadable board reports the error instead of claiming nothing to do', async ($, on) => {
  harness(on, () => {
    throw new Error('ENOENT: no such file')
  })
""","""test('an unreadable board reports the error instead of claiming nothing to do', async ($, on) => {
  // No fs.read stub on purpose: the real read of a board that is not there
  // fails for real. A hook that throws is skipped by the engine, so throwing
  // would have tested the harness rather than the mod.
  on('command.register', () => ({ value: undefined }))
  on('session.start', () => ({ cwd: '/work' }))
  on('ui.open', () => ({ value: { isPlaced: true } }))
  on('ui.render', ($, e) => ({ type: 'Text', props: e.props ?? {}, children: ['drawn by Claude Code'] }))

# todo-board

What Claude is working on, what is blocked, and — the part that earns the board
its place — **what is waiting on you**.

```

```

```
Todo board  4 waiting on you  5 in progress  2 queued  2 done

blocked (4) ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    entire-api main has 0 brain files. The server is a 10-PR stack

in progress (5) ──────────────────────────────────────────
> T-05 Goal 3 — brain efficiency (asked)
    13 procs / 554MB, 12 idle. fix/worker-says-why records WHY
```

`!` blocked · `>` in progress · `·` queued · `+` done.
`[you]` means it cannot move without a decision from you. `(asked)` means you
asked for it, rather than Claude adding it.

**Blocked sorts first, on purpose.** A blocked task is the one that needs
somebody; a board that buried it under in-progress work would be a worse
version of saying nothing. The count also rides the spinner, so a task waiting
on you is visible without opening anything.

Each row carries its **state**, not a description — what was measured, what is
actually in the way. A board of titles is a list, and nobody needs another list.

## The tasks are a file, not plugin state

They live in `.claude/todo-board.json`:

```json
{ "id": "T-05", "title": "...", "status": "doing",
  "owner": "claude", "source": "user", "note": "what is true right now" }
```

`status` is `todo | doing | blocked | done`, `owner` is `claude | user`,
`source` is `user | proactive`.

A plain file, deliberately. Claude updates the board with an ordinary file edit
mid-task — no tool call, no ceremony — and the board survives `/clear`,
`/resume` and a new session, which plugin state does not. The module only draws
it.

**A board that cannot be read says so.** It never renders an empty board on a
missing or malformed file: "nothing to do" and "I could not look" are different
claims, and the second one is the one that is true. Pinned by a test.

## Develop

```
claude plugin validate .
claude plugin test                      # 7 tests, every guard weakening-verified
node scripts/preview.mjs                # draw the real board outside Claude Code
```

`preview.mjs` imports `hooks/register.js` unmodified, so it cannot drift from
what the pane actually draws. The `node_modules/claude-code` stub beside it
exists only so that import resolves outside the host; `claude plugin test` uses
the real package and ignores it.

Both done.

## `/todo` — the board

Installed and rendering. Blocked sorts first on purpose, and the count rides the spinner so something waiting on you is visible without opening anything:

```
Todo board  4 waiting on you  5 in progress  3 queued  3 done

blocked (4) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
! T-06  Goal 4 — shared hosted brain  [you] (asked)
    entire-api main has 0 brain files. 10-PR stack, 1,824 commits + 97 migrations stale
! T-10  #329 and #321 are green and mergeable  [you]
    31 checks pass, 0 failures. One approval each
```

Tasks live in `.claude/todo-board.json` — a plain file, deliberately, so I update it with an ordinary edit mid-task and it survives `/clear`, `/resume` and new sessions, which plugin state doesn't. `[you]` marks what can't move without your decision; a done task stops counting against you. Each row carries *state*, not a description — a board of titles is a list, and you don't need another list. 7 tests, 5 weakenings red, validation clean. It **refuses to draw an empty board** on a missing or malformed file, because "nothing to do" and "I couldn't look" are different claims.

I seeded it with 15 real tasks and your standing instruction is now a memory, so new requests land on it in future sessions too.

## Fixing the brain-usage gap, proactively

You said fix it, so I did rather than just noting it. `brain-memory` now counts searches per turn and says **once**, in the transcript:

> `6 searches this turn, 0 brain calls — `entire brain brief "<task>"` answers "what do we already know about this" before the next one.`

Fires at 5+ searches, never when the turn already asked the brain, never twice in a turn, and resets per turn. The thresholds are the whole design: a couple of greps genuinely *is* cheaper than a retrieval round-trip, and nagging there is how a nudge gets muted. 5 weakenings, all red. 31 tests total.

That's the honest form of the fix — the guide is read once at session start and then everyone does what's fastest; this arrives while the choice is being made. Whether it actually changes my behaviour is now **T-14**, and `/brainusage` can measure it: retrieval calls per day, before versus after. I'm not claiming it works yet.

## Also landed since you last looked

`fix/bundle-sharing-truth` — the one teammate path that works today was silently destructive. `export` now prints the exact import command (`--sha256` is required and the digest was printed nowhere else), the refusal stopped advising a state a set-up brain can never be in, and an empty `recall` after an import names the import and its date instead of sending you to re-distill — which cannot restore what an import replaced. The trace comes from the semantic audit log, which already records `bundle_import`, so no manifest field and no schema bump. 4 weakenings red.

**Nine branches now, all local, nothing pushed.** Four things sit on your approval — they're on the board.

content.text: The test caught a real gap — my wrapper used `isUnknownFieldError`, which doesn't match the wrapped form. Let me check and use the robust predicate:

content.text: `isUnknownFieldError` uses `HasPrefix`, and the error arrives wrapped with `"parse brain manifest: …"` — so it never matched. That's why the remedy never appeared. Using the predicate that handles the wrapped form:

input.command:
cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/brain-worker-why
python3 - <<'PY'
p='internal/cli/brain.go'; s=open(p).read()
old = '''	manifest, _, err := readBrainManifest(outputDir, false)
	if isUnknownFieldError(err) {'''
new = '''	manifest, _, err := readBrainManifest(outputDir, false)
	// NOT isUnknownFieldError: that matches on a PREFIX, and by the time the
	// error reaches here it has been wrapped ("parse brain manifest: ..."), so
	// the prefix never matches and the remedy was silently never attached.
	if errRetiredManifestField(err) {'''
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new, 1)
# the message is now built in one place
old2 = '''		return manifest, fmt.Errorf("%w; this manifest carries a field this build retired, so writers cannot round-trip it without erasing what another build recorded -- rebuild it with `entire brain refresh --force`", err)'''
new2 = '''		return manifest, errors.New(retiredManifestFieldMessage(err))'''
assert old2 in s
s = s.replace(old2, new2, 1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print('fixed')
PY
grep -n '"errors"' internal/cli/brain.go >/dev/null || python3 -c "
p='internal/cli/brain.go'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('\t\"fmt\"','\t\"errors\"\n\t\"fmt\"',1); open(p,'w').write(s); print('errors import added')"
gofmt -w internal/cli/brain.go

Goal 3 now has a root cause, not just a symptom — and the instrument I built two commits earlier is what found it, in under a minute:

```
prepass_error: delta session export: parse brain manifest:
  memory_state_corrupt: brain manifest cannot be parsed:
  json: unknown field "suppressed_warnings"
```

`suppressed_warnings` appears **nowhere in the current tree**. It was retired without a schema bump, while every manifest the older build wrote still carries it. Writers refuse such a manifest *deliberately* — rewriting from a struct that never saw the field would erase what another build recorded — so the condition is **permanent**. The worker treated it as transient and relaunched on the 1m→30m chain, ~2 hours per repository, every attempt ending exactly where it started. Each pending retry is a live **sleeping process**, not a timer: 13 workers, 554 MB, twelve at 0.0% CPU. Six repos in that state at once, and the log said only `prepass_failed`.

Fixed on `fix/worker-says-why`: durable failures stop the chain at the first failure, the refusal names `entire brain refresh --force`, and readers still tolerate the field — availability is the reader's concern, not destroying state is the writer's, and collapsing that would take every query down with one retired field. Verified live on the real failing brain: `prepass_gave_up` false → true with the cause recorded.

Two things worth flagging about how that went:

- **My first attempt at the remedy silently did nothing.** I used `isUnknownFieldError`, which matches on a *prefix*, and the error arrives wrapped as `"parse brain manifest: …"` — so it never fired. The test caught it; reading the code did not.
- **It does not reproduce in a fresh throwaway repo.** A clean brain completes normally. I'd have concluded "not a product bug" if I'd stopped at the throwaway, which is exactly what I nearly did.

Also corrected: I'd said "every recent worker on this machine is failing". True of those six repos, not universal — a clean brain is fine.

**Board is at 17 tasks**, including two new ones I added rather than silently dropping: `T-16` round-trip unknown manifest fields (the principled fix that removes this whole failure class instead of handling one instance), and `T-17` repair the six brains already blacked out on this machine.

Telling detail — the `BrainVersion` field's own comment documents this exact hazard as known:

> *"omitempty, and never set on the on-disk brain manifest, so no stored manifest gains a field an older build would then refuse to rewrite."*

lines: +// daemonScopeSuffix distinguishes a daemon installed into an OVERRIDDEN unit
+// The label used to be derived from the daemon NAME alone, which is constant,
+// so every environment on a machine rendered the same label. The plist PATH was
+// isolated by ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_DIR and the LABEL was not, so `launchctl
+// bootstrap` of a throwaway unit REPLACED the real registration and repointed
+// it at a scratch binary in a directory about to be deleted. That happened
+// twice here in one day; the second time it took a bootout/bootstrap to undo.
+// Only an overridden directory gets a suffix. The default must keep rendering
+// the label it always has, or every existing install is orphaned on upgrade --
+// a migration this cannot justify when the whole point is not breaking things.
// systemdUnitName is the daemon name with the unit suffix; systemd unit names
// are already plain identifiers, so no transformation is needed.
func systemdUnitName(name string) string { return name + ".service" }
return daemonPlan{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot resolve home directory for the launchd agent")

Goal 3 now has **two** root causes fixed, and the second one only surfaced because I re-measured instead of declaring victory.

**The orphaned-brain case.** A brain outlives its repository — scratch clones, benchmark cells, a deleted checkout — and the worker kept relaunching against it: `not a git repository`. Nine orphans out of 47 on your machine, three holding **~2,650 recorded prepass failures each**, still failing after the manifest repair. I reproduced it by deleting a repo out from under its brain, so the error text is observed, not guessed. It now joins the durable class, with its own remedy — a retired field is repaired by `refresh --force`, an orphan by `reset`. Those are pinned apart by test, because sending an orphan to refresh fixes nothing and sending a repairable brain to reset would destroy it.

Three things worth telling you plainly:

**I made a real mistake.** My weakening patches were in double quotes, so bash executed the backticked commands inside them — that's why `entire brain reset` and a live `refresh --force` ran mid-test. No damage: `reset` refused without `--force`, both brains are intact with manifests, and the refresh was the same repair I'd already applied. I redid every affected weakening through patch files where nothing can be substituted.

**The weakening pass caught a bug the code review didn't.** Two guards stayed green when I broke them. Chasing why exposed that the remedy was being printed **twice** — `loadBrainManifestForReplace` attaches it, then the worker asked for the message again. It's idempotent now. And the branch that looked dead turned out to be load-bearing for the *bare* error the delta-export path actually produces — no fixture had covered that, which is precisely why it looked dead.

**I can't give you the clean worker number yet.** It's still inflated by the 11 index rebuilds I triggered, and the running daemon is the installed 0.1.0 binary with none of these fixes — which is why 27,233 failures carry no reason while only 3 do. That's the strongest argument for shipping this branch, and it's exactly what I can't do without you.

`fix/worker-says-why` is 4 commits, +679/−8 across 10 files. **Eleven branches, all local.** One new item for you on the board: `T-19`, the nine orphans still sitting there — clearing them means `reset`, which deletes brain data, so that's your call not mine.

input.description: Make printed remedies runnable
input.prompt:
WORKTREE: /Users/suhaan/devenv/brain-runnable-remedies (branch fix/runnable-remedies, based on fix/runnable-advice, NOT on main). Work ONLY there. Never cd to another checkout.

Repo: entireio/entire-brain (Go). Backlog row UX-21.

PROBLEM: ~106 user-facing strings hardcode `entire brain <verb>`. On a plugin-style install the runnable command is `entire-brain <verb>` (no space), so every one of those printed remedies is UNRUNNABLE for that user. They are told to run something that does not exist.

THE HELPER ALREADY EXISTS on this branch — do not invent another:
  internal/cli/setup_invocation.go
    brainInvocation(lookup tui.EnvLookup, verb string) string
      = setupBrainCommand(setupCommandPrefix(lookup)) + " " + verb
  Call sites elsewhere pass `os.LookupEnv` as the lookup. Read setup_invocation.go
  and at least three existing call sites BEFORE changing anything, and follow that
  pattern exactly.

SCOPE — convert a site ONLY when ALL of these hold:
  a) the string is shown to a user (an error, warning, hint, remedy, status//doctor line), AND
  b) it names a command the user is expected to RUN, AND
  c) a lookup is actually reachable at that point (a function with access to env/opts, or os.LookupEnv).

DO NOT convert:
  - comments, test files, testdata, docs/*.md
  - cobra `Long`/`Short`/`Example` help text built at package init or command-construction time where no lookup is available — changing those to a runtime call changes WHEN they are evaluated. If a help string is genuinely user-facing and a lookup IS available at construction, you may convert it, but say so explicitly in your report and treat it as a separate group.
  - any string where the literal `entire brain` is part of prose ABOUT the product rather than a command to run.
  - strings already using the helper.

For every site you deliberately skip, record the reason by category (not one line per site — group them).

RULES (non-negotiable):
1. NEVER push, open a PR, merge, or approve. Commit to the local branch only. No AI attribution footer in commit messages.
2. Every behaviour change needs a TEST, and each guard must be WEAKENING-VERIFIED: revert the production change compile-clean, run the test, capture the RED assertion text, restore, confirm green. A green suite is NOT evidence.
   There is strong prior art ON THIS BRANCH: `internal/cli/truthful_advice_test.go` contains TestEveryCommandPrintedInSourceResolves, which scans internal/cli for backticked `entire brain ...` spans and resolves them against the real cobra tree. READ IT FIRST and extend that pattern rather than inventing one. A good guard here asserts that a converted remedy renders with the plugin-style prefix when the env says so — i.e. drive it with a fake lookup, both ways.
3. NON-VACUITY: your test must fail if it matches nothing. Assert a floor on how many sites it checked.
4. CPU DISCIPLINE — the machine is under load from index rebuilds. Focused package only:

content.text:
`UX-21` verified independently — the guard fires with the exact file:line and a named fix, and the tree restores clean.

**What landed this round**

`fix/runnable-remedies` (stacked on `fix/runnable-advice`), 43 files, +244/−116: ~101 printed remedies now render in the reader's own dispatch spelling. A plugin-install user was previously told to run `entire brain refresh`, which on that install doesn't exist.

The agent's skip decisions were the interesting part, and they were right to skip:

- **MCP tool descriptions** — it converted them first, `TestMCPToolSurfaceGolden` went red because the golden would then vary with the shell's env, and it reverted. Correct call.
- **A persisted seed artifact** — the spelling is written into a file, so it must be deterministic, not reader-dependent.
- **The machine-readable capabilities contract** — pinned by a regression test for good reason.

Two it flagged as genuinely yours to decide: converting the MCP descriptions means regenerating that golden under a fixed env, and the **embedded agent guides** (`agentsetup/guide.go`, `strict.go`) still hardcode `entire brain` with no lookup plumbing — so the guide we ship to agents is itself unrunnable on a standalone install. That's the same defect one layer up.

**On the test failure.** The full-package run I did — the one the agent admitted it owed — came back with exactly one failure. I didn't trust either agent's "pre-existing" claim and checked: it fails *in isolation* on `fix/setup-status-output-truth`, a branch that never touched distill or ollama, and passes in isolation on the UX-21 branch while failing there only under parallel load. It's a timing-sensitive byte-ceiling assertion that overshoots by ~6 MB on a loaded box. Pre-existing flake, now a memory so the next full run doesn't send someone hunting through their own diff.

**Twelve branches, all local.** The board's remaining items are the six that need you — the hosted-server decision, three approvals, the core-type change I won't make solo, and clearing the orphans (which deletes brain data).

content.text:
`UX-30` done — three remedies that couldn't be followed, each verified against the built binary before I touched it:

- **`--graph-binary`** was offered as the way out of a provider failure, but it appears in **neither `setup --help` nor `refresh --help`** (zero occurrences each) — it only exists on `bench` and `entities`. The commands that hit the error don't accept the flag the error tells you to pass. Now both messages name `entire plugin install graph`, which the host CLI really offers and the index really lists as `graph`.
- **`scripts/install.sh` "from the entire-brain checkout… the sibling clone"** — a reader who installed the plugin has neither, and that's exactly who reaches this message.
- **"delete it and re-run"** was said for *every* unreadable setup record, including a permission error or a file briefly locked. The call site's own comment spells out the cost: every path below acts on a previous daemon identity, so a lost record can retire a watcher belonging to another repo. Only an unparseable record is unrecoverable now; a read failure says it may be temporary, names the file, and says not to delete it unless a re-run reports it unparseable.

Three things I'd rather flag than paper over:

**One of my guards didn't hold at first, and the reason was instructive.** The `--graph-binary` weakening stayed green because with the default binary the code returns *early* through the provider-missing branch and never reaches the lines I'd changed. The test was passing without exercising its subject. Fixed by driving it with a custom binary path plus a non-vacuity assert.

**A fourth weakening I'm not claiming.** The typed `fs.ErrPermission`/`ErrNotExist` check in `setupRecordIsCorrupt` is defensive only — the text fallback already declines those, so removing it changes nothing. I kept it for intent and said so in the commit rather than reporting 4/4.

**An existing test pinned the old advice.** It asserted `scripts/install.sh` while its own comment said the intent was "a missing plugin must name the install step". I updated it to that intent and added the inverse assertion, rather than deleting it.

`UX-23` (41 verbs, seven ways to ask a question) and `UX-29` (misleading names) are the last backlog items, and I've moved them to **your** column — both are breaking renames, not solo commits.

**Twelve branches, all local, all clean.** Everything still open on the board needs a decision from you.

import re

# ---- seed.go + semantic.go: take HEAD at every conflict ----
# HEAD is the install-ux side, which routes the paths through
# worktreeGateIgnore -- the GATE-only exemption (UX-08). Entire's own files must
# not block the install, and they must not be listed as blocking either.
for p in ('internal/cli/seed.go', 'internal/cli/semantic.go'):

    pat = re.compile(r'<<<<<<< HEAD\n(.*?)=======\n(.*?)>>>>>>> [^\n]*\n', re.S)
    for m in pat.finditer(s):

    out.append(s[i:])
    s = ''.join(out)
    assert '<<<<<<<' not in s, p
    open(p, 'w').write(s)

p = 'internal/cli/semantic.go'

decls = [m.start() for m in re.finditer(r'func dirtyWorktreeRefusal\(verb string, paths \[\]string\) error \{', s)]
assert len(decls) == 2, f'expected 2 declarations, found {len(decls)}'

assert s.count('func dirtyWorktreeRefusal(verb string, paths []string) error {') == 1

merge: reconcile the dirty-worktree refusal, keeping both halves

rewrote this refusal without knowing about the other. Both declared
`dirtyWorktreeRefusal` in semantic.go; neither exists on main. Merging them
naively produced a duplicate declaration that does not compile, and resolving
with -X theirs silently discarded one branch's fix.

They had fixed different halves:

  UX-08  the gate must not count Entire's OWN files as dirty -- our installers
         were blocking our installer -- and the refusal should say how many
         files and which, with correct singular/plural, summarising a long
         list rather than printing it.
  UX-05  the refusal must name `.brainignore`, the one escape hatch that
         appeared in no error string and no README line, and which would have
         cleared the live case that started this work.

Keeping either message alone loses a real fix, so the surviving message does
both. Path discovery goes through worktreeGateIgnore, the gate-only exemption,
so the paths NAMED are exactly the paths that actually blocked -- listing files
the gate already forgave would be its own small lie.

Both branches' existing suites pass unchanged: no test was edited to make this
merge work, which is the evidence that the combined message really satisfies
both intents rather than splitting the difference. A new test pins the two
halves together, because the failure mode here is a later edit dropping one and
still looking correct. describeDirtyWorktreePaths is removed, orphaned by the
merge.

Four weakenings, each red: dropping .brainignore, dropping the count, dropping
singular/plural, and disabling truncation.
EOF

- readers **tolerate** unknown fields

Also fixed: setup no longer claims "queryable" when seed *and* semantic both failed; `--no-daemon`/`--no-backfill` are remembered, so following our own "just re-run setup" advice stops silently installing a login service you declined; setup output went 52 → 34 lines by silencing the nested refresh that was leaking through.

## Goal 2 — simplify docs and complicated things ✅ *built, not merged*

`doctor` went **40 lines → 7**, measured on your repo, every line ending in a command you can actually run. Dead flags deleted, the docs contract made bidirectional so an undocumented verb now fails CI, ~120 printed remedies now render in your install's spelling, and three remedies that were literally impossible to follow are gone — including one that told you to pass `--graph-binary`, a flag that appears in neither `setup --help` nor `refresh --help`.

**Two rows left, and they're yours:** UX-23 (41 verbs, seven ways to ask a question) and UX-29 (misleading names) are breaking renames, not solo commits.

## Goal 3 — brain efficiency ✅ *built, and your machine is already repaired*

This is the one with a live result. Two root causes:

1. A manifest field retired without a schema bump made brains **permanently unwritable**, driving a 1m→30m retry chain, ~2h per repo, each pending retry a live sleeping process. **11 brains were in this state — including `devenv` and `entire-brain`, blacked out since Oct 6.** All 11 repaired. That part is real and already in effect.
2. Orphaned brains whose repo is gone retried forever — 3 of them with ~2,650 recorded failures each.

Measured: prepass failures **continuous → 0**, blacked-out manifests **11 → 0**.

## Goal 4 — shared hosted brain showing teammates' facts ❌ **not done**

Blocked, and not by me. `entire-api` main has **zero** brain files and zero brain routes. The server is a 10-PR stack **1,824 commits and 97 migrations** behind main. `/brainusage` (month heatmap + bar chart) and `/todo` are both built, tested and installed — **they need a Claude Code restart** to appear, since mods register at session start.

import re

p = 'internal/httpapi/router.go'
s = open(p).read()
m = re.search(r'<<<<<<< HEAD\n(.*?)=======\n(.*?)>>>>>>> [^\n]*\n', s, re.S)
assert m, 'router conflict missing'
head, theirs = m.group(1), m.group(2)
rest = s[:m.start()] + s[m.end():]
wanted = [l for l in theirs.split('\n') if l.strip().startswith('"')]
keep = []
for line in wanted:
    path = line.strip().strip('"')
    # already imported elsewhere in the file? then adding it again breaks the build
    if re.search(r'^\s*"' + re.escape(path) + r'"\s*$', rest, re.M):

    keep.append(line)
resolved = head + '\n'.join(keep) + ('\n' if keep else '')
s = s[:m.start()] + resolved + s[m.end():]

head_keys = set(re.findall(r'^\s*"([A-Za-z0-9_]+)":', head, re.M))

s = s[:m.start()] + resolved + s[m.end():]

24 pull requests and 253 commits since 0.1.0.

**Not ready to ship as-is.** `connect`, `publish` and `facts sync` are visible
commands for a hosted brain whose server does not exist on `entire-api` main —
a reader who installs this finds commands that cannot work. Decide whether to
hide them or document them as unavailable before tagging. See "Known gaps".

### Added

- **Documents beyond Markdown.** PDF, Word, Excel and PowerPoint are read into
  the brain.
- **A REST API, with Python and TypeScript clients.**
- **MCP over HTTP**, opt-in and authenticated, alongside the existing stdio
  transport.
- **`brain_remember` over MCP**: an agent can record a durable fact without
  shelling out to the CLI.
- **Webhooks**: notify another service when the brain changes.
- **Facts as plain Markdown files**, written out for reading and diffing.
- **Cross-repository facts**: remember something that is not about one repo.
- **Memory import from another tool.**
- **Time-weighted retrieval ranking.**
- **`brain stop` / `brain start`** to pause background work machine-wide.
- **Hosted sync client** — `brain connect`, per-sync token mint, pull-into-local,
  daemon and hook wiring (COR-2030/COR-2031). See "Known gaps".
- **Benchmarks**: `memory-ladder`, a five-condition probe of agent memory
  surfaces, and index size / query latency measured against codebase size.

### Changed

- `brief --json` puts facts and history before status, and the guides name
  `recall`.
- Developer commands are hidden from the default help.
- `factmerge` is exported for the brainstore service (COR-2023).
- Semantic generations are verified once per file version rather than once per
  query.

### Fixed

- `remember` returns the persisted merged fact in JSON.
- An empty fact query names the branches that do hold facts.
- The ollama chunk-size limits are real, and the advice that breaks them is
  corrected.

### Documentation

- A contributor concepts guide.
- What the install script does, rather than what it is not.
- What we measure, what we found, and what we do not claim.

### Known gaps

- **Hosted brain has no server.** The client half ships here; `entire-api` main
  has no brain routes. `connect`, `publish` and `facts sync` are therefore
  inert. The server is an unmerged 10-PR stack; its publish half builds against
  current main, its fact-sync half imports three packages main deleted
  deliberately, and its five migrations are dated before 43 that have already
  shipped, so goose would skip them on a deployed database.
- **Sharing a brain is lossy.** `bundle import --overwrite` replaces the
  receiver's fact layer rather than merging it. The import now says so at the
  moment it happens, but one-way copy is the only sharing that works today.

'''
s = s.replace(old, new, 1)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('changelog written')
PY

Definitive. **brainstore is deployed** — Aurora provisioned in:

- **Prod (5 regions):** `us-east-2`, `eu-west-2`, `eu-central-1`, `ap-south-1`, `ap-southeast-2`
- **Nonprod/staging (3):** `eu-west-1`, `us-east-2`, `us-west-2`

And `entire.io` has the BFF client wired in (`api/src/lib/brainstore.ts`, called from `routes/trails.ts`, behind a feature flag).

**My root error:** I analysed `entirehq/entire-api`, which is `archived: true` — frozen 2026-09-17. One API field I never checked. Everything I concluded about goal 4 came from a dead repo. Let me correct what I've written, because it's actively misleading now:

input.command:

---
name: brain-not-on-api-main
description: "CORRECTED: entirehq/entire-api is ARCHIVED. brainstore IS deployed — Aurora in 5 prod regions and 3 nonprod. Never analyse that repo again; check `archived` before trusting any repo's main"
metadata:
  type: project
---

**This note previously said the hosted brain had no server. That was WRONG, and
it misled a long session.** Corrected 2026-10-12 after the user pushed back.

## What is actually true

**brainstore is DEPLOYED.** `entirehq/infra` provisions Aurora for it:

- **prod (5):** `us-east-2`, `eu-west-2`, `eu-central-1`, `ap-south-1`,
  `ap-southeast-2`
- **nonprod (3):** `eu-west-1`, `us-east-2`, `us-west-2`

`entirehq/entire.io` carries the BFF client: `api/src/lib/brainstore.ts`, called
from `api/src/routes/trails.ts`, with a flag in `frontend/src/lib/featureFlags.ts`.

## The mistake, so it is not repeated

**`entirehq/entire-api` is ARCHIVED** (`archived: true`, frozen 2026-09-17).
Its `main` has no brain code and PRs #744-#752/#242 sit open forever because the
repo is dead, not because the work was abandoned. I analysed that repo for
hours, measured "1,824 commits behind", built a release-blocker argument on it,
and repeated "the hosted brain has no server" many times.

Three compounding errors:

1. **Never checked whether the repo was alive.** `gh api repos/<org>/<repo>
   --jq .archived` is one call. A main that has not moved in four weeks while
   sibling repos move hourly is the tell.
2. **Confused "not on main" with "not deployed".** Source state says nothing
   about what runs in production. Deployment lives in `entirehq/infra`.
3. **Searched only the repo I assumed.** `gh api 'search/code?q=brainstore+org:entirehq'`
   found it immediately — 54 matches, including every Aurora module.

## How to apply

- Before concluding anything from a repo's `main`, check `archived` and when it
  last moved.
- To answer "is X deployed", search `entirehq/infra`, not the service repo.
- `entire-api`'s successor for product work is not yet identified here; the
  active repos are `entiredb`, `strata`, `fleet`, `entire-records`, `entire.io`.

Related: [[unseen-is-not-impossible]] — this is that failure exactly: I upgraded
"I have not found it" into "it does not exist", repeatedly, and only stopped when
told.
EOF
python3 - <<'PY'
p='/Users/suhaan/.claude/projects/-Users-suhaan-devenv/memory/MEMORY.md'
s=open(p).read()
old=[l for l in s.split('\n') if l.startswith('- [brain not on api main]')][0]
new="- [brain not on api main — CORRECTED](brain-not-on-api-main.md) — entire-api is ARCHIVED; brainstore IS DEPLOYED (5 prod + 3 nonprod Aurora regions, BFF client in entire.io). Check `archived` before trusting any repo's main"
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s); print('memory corrected')
PY

Corrected everywhere — memory, board, and changelog.

**What I got wrong:** `entirehq/entire-api` is **archived**, frozen 2026-09-17. I spent hours analysing a dead repo — measuring "1,824 commits behind", costing a "stack revival", building a release blocker — and repeated "the hosted brain has no server" many times. One API field (`archived`) would have stopped all of it. A `main` that hasn't moved in four weeks while sibling repos move hourly was the tell, and I read it as "stale stack" instead of "dead repo."

Three compounding mistakes, all mine:

1. Never checked whether the repo was alive.
2. Treated "not on main" as "not deployed" — deployment lives in `entirehq/infra`, which I never searched.
3. Searched only the repo I'd assumed. `search/code?q=brainstore+org:entirehq` returns 54 matches and finds it instantly.

That's the exact failure my own notes warn about: upgrading "I haven't found it" into "it doesn't exist," and only stopping when told.

**So, on your actual question — ready for a release once the PR merges?**

Closer than I said, but one real check remains, and it's now a *different* one. Goals 1–3 are done and `integration/brain-ux` is green. The changelog is drafted (24 PRs, 253 commits). The hosted commands **do** have a live server, so they're not inert — but I've never exercised `connect` → `facts sync` against a real cell, precisely because I'd convinced myself there was nothing to connect to. That's `T-21` on the board and it's mine, not yours.

Want me to run that end-to-end against a cell now? It's the last thing I'd want verified before tagging, and it'd also tell us whether the "bundle import replaces facts" limitation still matters — `facts sync` may merge properly where bundles don't.
